doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Early gigs, Max Roach, leaving Detroit
title: Leaving Detroit with the musicians, 1960, and dating Clifford Brown's death
summary: Most Detroit musicians left when he did in 1960; he and Graves settle Clifford Brown's death year as 1956.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: 1960, when I joined Cannonball. See most of the musicians left when I left, ‘cause they were closely associated with me. Mostly all the musicians. Bennie Maupin, all them – all them cats. In some way, they were connected to me. I saw Bennie Maupin, he almost cried seeing me. He hadn’t seen me in years, and um – a lot of those cats, they came. When we were younger, probably Kenny Durrell and Tommy Flannigan were the best young musicians – the bebop kind of musicians, and they were young, you know.
And did Mr. Flannigan go to New York before you or after you, or around the same time?
It might have been before me. Yeah, Tommy might have left before me.
I believe that Mr. Clifford Brown passed on in – I think Mr. Brown passed on in 1956.
Was it – that’s what it says? It shouldn’t have been.
